_clause_text_note: SUBSTITUTION, ACCEPTED AT R79/S81.1. Records carry a clause LINE RANGE plus a DIGEST, not a copy of the clause text. THE REASON IS SINGLE-SOURCE, NOT ACCURACY: a copy of the clause text inside these records would be a RESTATEMENT of SCHEMA_SET_FINAL.md, and this project has spent thirty rounds establishing what restatements do - they fork. The range-plus-digest keeps one authority for the clause text and makes every reader of these records go to it. (Accuracy is a side benefit: transcription error becomes impossible. It is not the reason.) The generator emits the FULL CLAUSE TEXT into the diff, because an author cannot approve a digest.
_digest_normalisation: EXPLICIT, per R79/S81.2. SCHEMA_SET_FINAL.md is CRLF ON DISK (2479 CRLF, 0 bare LF). Each clause_sha256 is NOT a digest of those bytes. It is: read the file with universal newlines (Python text mode, which converts CRLF to LF), split on LF, take lines [clause_first_line-1 : clause_last_line], join with a single LF, encode UTF-8, NO trailing newline, sha256. For SC-1 (l.161-203) the three candidates differ: LF-joined no-trailing-NL = a50f2323... (STORED); LF-joined with trailing NL = 26c9a099...; CRLF-joined = f3512a2c.... A digest whose normalisation is implicit is a defect waiting for the next tooling change, so it is written down here.
_repin_procedure: REQUIRED, per R79/S81.3, written now rather than when needed. If SCHEMA_SET_FINAL.md is legitimately edited, clause ranges are recomputed by LOCATING CLAUSE HEADERS - never by offset arithmetic. Procedure: (1) find each '### SC-<id> - ' header line; (2) within that clause, find its '**THE CLAUSE.**' line, which is clause_first_line; (3) clause_last_line is the line before the next line matching '^\*\*(DATA THE DECLARATION MUST SUPPLY|ROWS COVERED|INSERTION TEXT|INSERTION POINT|SUPERSESSION)' or the next '### SC-' header, whichever comes first; (4) recompute clause_sha256 under _digest_normalisation; (5) re-run verify_schema_records.py, which must report ALL CHECKS PASS. Offset arithmetic is forbidden because it assumes all change is displacement - the assumption that produced H-L17, and that produced four separate re-anchor failures in this project.
